provenance: Authored in-repo for Bruriah. Original prose, not derived from third-party skills.

limitations: A probe checks your tests, not your thinking: it cannot tell you whether the invariant you pinned is the right one.
Passing every probe you thought of says nothing about the invariants you did not name.
skills.provenance: Bruriah first-party pack; prose authored in-repo.
skills.summary: Break an invariant on purpose and confirm the test fails, so you know the test protects something rather than merely passing.

limitations: Verification shows what happened once, in one environment; it does not establish stability across platforms or untried inputs.
Running something successfully proves it ran, never that it is correct.
skills.provenance: Bruriah first-party pack; prose authored in-repo.
skills.summary: Execute the claim before stating it, especially numbers, commands and examples destined for documentation.

limitations: Protects only against the values you anticipated.
Costs future flexibility, and the cost is paid by whoever needs the case you closed.
Some constraints genuinely cannot be expressed structurally; forcing it produces worse designs than the checks it replaces.
skills.provenance: Bruriah first-party pack; prose authored in-repo.
skills.summary: Prefer designs where an invalid state cannot be written down over checks that reject it, and know when a check is the honest tool instead.

limitations: Preserving behaviour is not preserving quality: a faithful extraction of a bad design is a well-organised bad design.
Zero tests modified only proves as much as the suite covers; untested behaviour can be rewritten silently.
skills.provenance: Bruriah first-party pack; prose authored in-repo.
skills.summary: Refactor so that no test file needs editing, and treat the order in which checks fail as behaviour worth pinning first.

limitations: Finds deadlines that live in the code; external ones (token sunsets, API deprecations) need a calendar, not a test.
Tells you where a deadline is and what it takes down, never whether the deadline is correct.
skills.provenance: Bruriah first-party pack; prose authored in-repo.
skills.summary: Inject the clock and sweep it forward to find code that is correct today and broken on a date nobody wrote down.

limitations: A good description is necessary and nowhere near sufficient; it cannot fix a capability that is genuinely hard to explain.
It does not prove anyone uses the feature -- the only real evidence is watching someone who did not build it try.
skills.provenance: Bruriah first-party pack; prose authored in-repo.
skills.summary: Read your published interface as a stranger would: a capability nobody can find out how to call does not exist, and no test will report it.
